chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Everything with which you speak to Allah during the obligatory prayer, there is no problem (with it).

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What can be recited as supplication during obligatory prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Reported by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in al-Kafi, this hadith clarifies that the supplications recited within the obligatory prayer are not limited to specific fixed texts, allowing for personal invocation. This ruling underscores the flexibility of the 'Qunut' or internal du'a in Shia jurisprudence, encouraging believers to engage directly with Allah in their own words during the standing position of prayer. It reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the spiritual intimacy and accessibility of prayer beyond rigid formalism.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Hammad Bin Isa, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Everything what you speak to Allahazwj with during an Obligatory Salāt, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whatever (words) with which you speak to Allah in Salah (prayer) is not harmful.’” (Ahadith 4-5 of this Chapter are best explained by fatwas.)
